claims: For those born in 1960 or later, full retirement age is 67.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1954 or earlier is 65–66.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1955–1959 is 66 and 2–10 months.
Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1960 or later is 67.
Social Security benefits can start at 62 but are permanently reduced.
Delayed retirement increases benefits by ~8% annually up to age 70.
Social Security replaces approximately 40% of the average wage earner's income.
It is possible to work and receive benefits while retired.
Social Security benefits may be temporarily reduced if under full retirement age and earn over a certain limit.
